Episode 246. The Battle for the Mitra Desert (16)
Vahn's sword energy narrowly passed by Shimat.
Unconsciously, Shimat gripped his hand tightly in that moment. A keen sensation was telling him that this sword energy was on a completely different level from the one he had just fended off.
Although Elona had already distanced herself from the rift considerably, she turned her head abruptly, sensing the unexpected incoming sword energy.
'Damn it...!'

She had not anticipated that the Plutonian from beyond the rift would have such accurate targeting. She believed that if she moved behind the airborne fortresses, the Red Plutonian would inadvertently become a shield.
Instinctively, she expanded her protective barrier.
However, the barrier she thrust forward started distorting the moment the sword energy touched it.
It was a protective barrier formed by pulling the majority of Elona's magical power in an instant. She couldn't comprehend how it was breaking so easily.
'From a distance, crossing dimensions, this attack breaks my barrier...?'
Layer upon layer of her barriers were shattered almost instantaneously. As the sword energy approached, Elona screamed and thrust out her staff.
At the tip of the staff, a concentrated mass of magic energy glowed. Initially in a spherical shape, it split in half when colliding with the sword energy.
Between the split spheres, a tug-of-war ensued, with both Vahn's and Elona's energies pushing against each other.
In a way, it was a simple test of strength.
The tension was palpable, with no clear side having the upper hand. But once the balance tipped, it would undoubtedly sway irreversibly to one side.
Whirring, buzzing sounds filled the air.

Right in front of the staff, where the two energies clashed, the space warped like dough. Nearby enemy ships became unstable, swaying due to the push and pull of the forces. If it weren't for the protection of the airborne fortresses, those ships would have spun wildly before their engines exploded.
A low groan escaped Elona's lips. The staff in her hands trembled, and cold sweat dripped from her body.
One wrong move and she'd be slashed.
She was certain of it. She might not die, but it was clear that she wouldn't be able to return to the desert for a while.
'I should've dodged with full power from the start. A mistake, indeed. I may have to rely more on the Holy Crown.'
The Holy Crown.
When she had discussed with Jin earlier, she had said she saw 'no reason to leave it.' But in reality, Elona had been trying to avoid relying on the power of the Holy Crown as much as possible.
To communicate with the Tower of Tales. The more she relied on the Holy Crown, it seemed like the tower was trying to distance itself from her.
Whizz...
The Holy Crown split and wrapped new rings around her wrists and ankles. The Milky Way flowing in her eyes darkened further.
Then, little by little, the sword energy that was encroaching towards Elona began to be pushed back. The magical sphere holding the sword energy closed like the jaws of a beast.
There was a crunching, blunt noise, as if it wasn't the sword energy but flesh and bone being crushed.
Malice.
The method the Holy Crown chose to empower Elona was malice. The sphere ferociously tore at the sword energy as if trying to sever the artery of a living creature.
Nevertheless, for a while, the sword energy maintained its shape. It did not sever, nor scatter, but continued to target Elona.
15 seconds, a short time, but long for the obstructed sword energy to endure.
Eventually, Vahn's sword energy dispersed. Elona gasped for breath, looking down at the shattered fragments of the sword energy falling to the ground.
Suddenly amplifying her power through the Holy Crown made her feel dizzy and nauseous. Her vision blurred for a moment, and there was a spasm in her hand holding the staff.
The malice implanted by the Holy Crown didn't subside immediately. Even after Vahn's sword energy dispersed, Elona had to endure the surging malice.

She wanted to rush beyond the rift and kill everyone inside. Or, she wanted to annihilate the Red Plutonian fleet indiscriminately. If not for Kelliark's order to aid in destroying the passage, she would have gone berserk.
In the process of calming her inner turmoil, she missed it. A fragment of the sword energy she thought had completely vanished lunged at her heart.
"Cough...!"
That fragment pierced through Elona's protective barrier and through her shoulder. Had she reacted even slightly slower, it would have pierced her heart.
Elona quickly channeled her magic into the wound, trying to seal the turbulent energy within.
'It's dangerous here, I need to go to the tower to heal...!'
Elona looked up at Shimat.
Fortunately, he had no intention of attacking her at the moment.

Rather, one could say his intentions had lessened even more. Considering Gaila and Uss's situation, Shimat should have attacked the injured Elona, but the recent attack from Lafrarosa made it clearer.
Now was the time to join hands with her and Zipple.
'If that sword energy targeted me instead of Elona Zipple.'
Of course, the form of the sword energy would have been different since it would need to attack multiple people, but Shimat and the Red Plutonian would surely have suffered more.
It was a wiser decision to join hands with an enemy rather than to stand by and watch such a monster be released into the world.
Gritting his teeth...!
On one hand, he felt a sense of humiliation.
The second sword energy was proof that the descendant of the Blue Plutonian had judged Elona to be more dangerous than the Red Plutonian.
"This damn thing...!"
Shimat clenched his teeth and pulled up his Energy Waves. The air fortresses also boosted their power, focusing around the glowing heart, red as fresh blood.
Just as all energies converged on Lekan when Vahn unleashed the final strike, Tetalon instantly absorbed all the red energy waves scattered across the desert.
"Trapped, yet you dare to intimidate us! Before you emerge from that dark dimension, I'll tear you apart...!"
Red Plutonian Battle God Sword Technique:
Red Heavenly God Sword - Red Sea
Shimat hurled himself toward Lafrarosa's rift.
It seemed like a red meteor had fallen. Due to the various massive forces that had clashed thus far, horrifying shockwaves were continuously erupting from within the rift.
Every time Tetalon emitted a red light, the shockwaves were cleanly sliced. Shimat bravely charged into the torn shockwaves.
His intention was to unleash the Red Sea, the sea of red waves energy, into Lafrarosa.
He was certain that while the Battle God like Vahn might survive, the lesser Plutonian would surely not remain unscathed.
"As descendants of Blue Plutonian, you all are far from the cold-blooded like us! Feel it, no matter how formidable your power, you cannot protect everything. Your kin will die before your eyes!"
Kztz-Zing!
Tetalon pierced the dimensional rift. Due to the recoil, Shimat's body was covered in bulging veins, bursting and spewing blood.
Yet, Shimat did not let go of the sword embedded in the rift. Tetalon's blade was inducing a tidal wave of red energy inside.
Even Vahn in her prime, undoubtedly the strongest in Genesis Level, could not emit a more massive force than Shimat now.
It was because Shimat didn't unleash his sword with his power alone. The four air fortresses connected to him supplied him with energy.
The red energy waves, so vast that it filled and overflowed the entire desert, was infiltrating Lafrarosa through that tiny rift.
Shimat was imagining what lay beyond.
He pictured the descendants of Blue Plutonian struggling and spitting blood from the other dimension. Their Battle God would surely feel anger and helplessness at the sight of their dying kin.
He was convinced of it.
Shimat suddenly noticed that the dimensional rift was closing.
{God Brother! The rift has closed.}

Limagas, who had been analyzing the waves all along, communicated to Shimat. The rift was already completely closed, and the thunderous power of the Divine Sword that Shimat had been pouring out was sweeping across the desert and advancing.
'Damn it!'
Once again, only the descendants of Blue Plutonian were blessed.
It was not easy to regain composure. Having given up even the opportunity to harm Elona, he had counterattacked with all his power and the energy from the four airborne fortresses.
He never expected to fail so vainly. It wasn't that the opponent had skillfully fended him off, nor that he hadn't attacked properly due to his incompetence.
The door had simply closed unexpectedly.
From the beginning, the path through Lafrarosa was like this. It would suddenly open when unwanted, turning things upside down, and now, in the most annoying moment, it closed.
Thunk, thud!
Swollen veins protruded, and blood oozed from between his lips. Shimat barely clung to his sanity and began to retrieve the scattered power that was spreading endlessly across the desert.
“…Immediately initiate subspace tracking. And convey my opinion to Zipple right away. I won’t attack until Lafrarosa is destroyed, so make sure Elona Zipple doesn’t end up alone like today.”
{Yes.}

"Also, ask them to send more skilled people besides the Elona Zipple. The Zipple, those bug-like creatures, also need to prevent the liberation of Lafrarosa. Especially after today, they'll realize it even more painfully."
{Understood, God brother.}
Soon, Shimat spat out a mouthful of black blood and looked over the desert, where the Red Sea of the Divine Sword was heading.
As if on cue, Sribi, Karmashu, and Masalrun revealed themselves beyond the sandstorm.
[Oh, Shimat. That sword just now was really amazing, huh? But what now? It was meant to pierce Lafrarosa, that’s a pity.]
[Why don't you give us that power instead of just retrieving it? We've been absorbing it diligently, but we lacked time. Thanks to that, our flesh and bones have bonded so well. Look, look.]
[Masalrun doesn't care one way or another. From now on, I will curse you all again, so remember that.]
With a throbbing headache, Shimat returned to the bridge of Pibil. Those guys were still the terrible ghosts he couldn't attack or kill.
Looking back at everything that happened before the great seal, he felt that there were hardly any days as crappy as today.
